subject: physics
title: Newton's first law
key_idea: If the resultant force on an object is zero, a stationary object stays at rest and a moving object keeps the same velocity. The velocity only changes when a resultant force acts. That changes the speed, the direction, or both.

sections.heading: When the resultant force is zero

blocks.text: Newton's first law says what happens to an object when the forces on it are balanced. This section covers objects at rest and objects moving steadily.

items.meaning: The single force that has the same effect as all the forces on an object added together.

items: If the resultant force on a stationary object is zero, it **stays stationary**.
If the resultant force on a moving object is zero, it keeps moving at the **same speed and in the same direction**.
So a moving object with no resultant force keeps the same velocity.

blocks.text: This means no resultant force is needed to keep an object moving at a steady velocity. When a vehicle travels at a steady speed, the resistive forces balance the driving force.

items: Zero resultant force means no change in velocity.
A stationary object stays at rest. A moving object keeps the same speed and direction.
At a steady speed, driving force equals resistive force.

sections.heading: When the resultant force is not zero

blocks.text: Newton's first law also tells you when motion changes. The velocity of an object only changes if a resultant force acts on it.

items: A resultant force can change the **speed**, the **direction**, or both.
A resultant force in the direction of motion speeds the object up.
A resultant force against the direction of motion slows it down.
A resultant force at an angle to the motion changes its direction.

diagram.alt: Pick a situation to see the resultant force and what happens to the motion.

options.label: Car at a steady speed on a straight road
results: Zero: the driving force equals the resistive forces
options.explanation: The forces are balanced, so the velocity does not change.

options.label: Parked car
options.explanation: A stationary object stays stationary when the resultant force is zero.

options.label: Cyclist pedals harder: driving force bigger than resistive force
results: Forwards, in the direction of travel
options.explanation: The forces are unbalanced, so the speed changes.

options.label: Bowling ball rolling along a lane
results: Backwards: the resistive force acts opposite to the velocity
options.explanation: Friction and air resistance are the only horizontal forces on the ball.

options.label: Glider on a frictionless air-track after the push ends
options.explanation: With no resultant force, the glider keeps its velocity.

options.label: Car going round a bend at a steady speed
results: Not zero: it acts sideways, at an angle to the motion
The direction changes, so the velocity changes
options.explanation: A resultant force can change direction as well as speed.

items: A resultant force changes the velocity: the speed, the direction, or both.
Slowing down needs a resultant force too. Friction or air resistance does this.
Explain by comparing the forces: balanced means constant velocity, unbalanced means a change.

checks.q: A car moves at a constant 20 m/s on a straight road. What is the resultant force, and how do the driving force and resistive force compare?
checks.a: The resultant force is zero. The driving force equals the resistive force.

checks.q: A glider is pushed along a horizontal air-track with no friction and then let go. Describe its motion.
checks.a: It moves at a constant velocity, because there is no resultant force on it.

checks.q: A swimmer has a forward force of 50 N and a resistive force of 50 N. The forward force increases. What happens?
checks.a: The swimmer accelerates because the forces are unbalanced (forward force greater than resistive force).

worked_example.question:
The stone has just entered the water. As the stone moves through the water, it slows to a constant velocity.

Explain why the stone slows to a constant velocity as it moves through the water.
answer_points: So there is a resultant force acting in the opposite direction to the velocity, causing deceleration
As the velocity decreases, the drag decreases
Until drag is equal to weight, so the velocity is constant
worked_example.tip: Four marks, one for each step of the explanation. Drag can be called a resistive or frictional force. Ignore upthrust.

worked_example.question:
A cupcake case is falling at a constant velocity.

State the value of the acceleration of the cupcake case when it is falling at a constant velocity.
worked_example.tip: Ignore the word 'constant' and ignore units.

worked_example.question:
A teacher uses an air-track for motion experiments. Using the air-track means that there is no friction between the glider and the air-track.

The teacher places the glider on the horizontal air-track and gives it a small push to start it moving.

Explain the motion of the glider.
answer_points: The glider accelerates during the push
Then it moves at a constant (steady, uniform) speed or velocity
Because there are no other horizontal (unbalanced) forces acting on it
Or: there is a slight deceleration due to air resistance
worked_example.tip: Any two of the four points score the 2 marks.
